title: Spatial capture-recapture of leopard (Panthera pardus) at 100 camera traps in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, Sept 2021 to Jan 2022
creator: Curveira-Santos, Goncalo; Dupont, Gates; Sutherland, Chris; Gigliotti, Laura
citation: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., & Gigliotti, L. (2025). Data and Code for: Optimizing Camera-Trap Survey Designs for Multi-Species Density Estimation Using Spatial Capture-Recapture Models. OSF. https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/Y3W6F
abstract: Daily camera-trap detections of individually identified leopard (Panthera pardus) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy (Phinda), KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, 17 September 2021 to 11 January 2022: 60 cameras placed for leopards and 40 for small-bodied carnivores by the authors' two-stage design optimisation. One row per individual x operating camera-day; the deposited camera operation matrix is the survey set. Sibling tables for the other five identifiable carnivores of the same survey: curveirasantos_2026_phinda_cheetah_scr, curveirasantos_2026_phinda_lion_scr, curveirasantos_2026_phinda_hyena_scr, curveirasantos_2026_phinda_genet_scr, curveirasantos_2026_phinda_serval_scr. Trap coordinates are centred on the array (local metres) because three of the six species are IUCN Vulnerable.
samplingProtocol: Paired or single camera traps at 100 sites (Cuddeback and Spartan), checked over 117 calendar days; individuals identified from coat pattern (flank recorded as both / left / right where applicable), lions and cheetahs also by pride or coalition. Detection history is individual x camera x day.
surveyEvidenceNote: MYW2021_cam_op_site_effort_UTM.csv gives each camera site x day as 1 (operating), 0 (deployed, not operating) or NA (not deployed); a camera-day is surveyed iff 1 (4,470 of 11,700). Every detection falls on an operating camera-day. MYW43 never operated and has no rows.
closure: period (one season, Sept 2021 to Jan 2022, treated as closed by the authors)
geographicCoverage: Munywana Conservancy (Phinda Private Game Reserve), KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa; camera array centroid -27.9, 32.2 (0.1 degree); trap positions in __traps as local metres centred on the array
crs: local: metres, UTM 36S (EPSG:32736) easting/northing minus the array centroid (processor-centred)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: trap coordinates centred on the array centroid by the processor (local metres; exact UTM 36S positions withheld) because leopard, cheetah and lion (IUCN VU) share the one camera array; the centroid is given at 0.1 degree in geographicCoverage

designNote: Experimental list of E9: spatial capture-recapture with a trap key and __traps. Closed population, one session; occasion = calendar day as in the authors' oSCR code (they collapse occasions to counts with effort). One species per table (ruling #20); the six tables share traps and survey set.
notes: unit_flank_profile = the set of flanks ever recorded for the individual; single-flank ids may duplicate an animal recorded on the other flank.

notShipped.output/: simulation designs, simulation results (out_df_1..6.csv) and fitted oSCR null models: analysis outputs
notShipped.R/: the authors' oSCR fitting and simulation code
notShipped.spatial/Full_Phinda_2018_UTM.*: reserve fence shapefile, the SCR state space (analysis input)
notShipped.MYW_grid_cam_allocation.csv: identical to the Grid_Allocation column of the operation file (asserted); in __traps
notShipped.exact_coordinates: UTM 36S trap positions withheld (VU taxa); __traps carries them centred on the array
